paragraphs.text: Fascinated by the lore of ancient struggles, the archaeologist searches incessantly for remnants of an earlier, more powerful era.
Benalia has a complex caste system that changes with the lunar year. No matter what the season, the only caste that cannot be attained by either heredity or money is that of the hero.
"Such innocent little birds. They sing a sweet song, sitting on their fragile branch." —Grandmother Sengir
Glory surged through her and radiance surrounded her. All things were possible with the blessing of the Divine.
Tervish never noticed that the amulet had vanished. It had disappeared not only from his possession, but from his memory as well.
Sometimes it's best to let sleeping dragons lie.
"On this site where Kjeld's blood was spilled, let none raise a fist or deny a beggar." —Halvor Arenson, Kjeldoran priest
"The Hand of Justice will come to cleanse the world if we are true." —Oliver Farrel
"Bathed in hallowed light, the infidels looked upon the impurities of their souls and despaired." —The Book of Tal
To become an officer, an Icatian soldier had to pass a series of tests. These evaluated not only fighting and leadership skills, but also integrity, honor, and moral strength.
Icatia's once peaceful towns faced increasing attacks from orcs and goblins as the climate cooled. By the time the empire fell, they were little more than armed camps.
"With a great cry, the goblin host broke and ran as the first wave of knights penetrated its ranks." —Tivadar of Thorn, History of the Goblin Wars

Before a woman marries in the village of Sursi, she must visit the land of the mesa pegasus. Legend has it that if the woman is pure of heart and her love is true, a mesa pegasus will appear, blessing her family with long life and good fortune.
The purpose of any moat is to impede attack. Some are filled with water, some with thistles. Some are filled with things best left unseen.
"Trained to battle the followers of Tourach, the Order of Leitbur was not as successful in later conflicts with orcish and goblin raiders." —*Sarpadian Empires, vol. I*
What walks on four legs in the morning, two legs in the afternoon, and three legs in the evening?
Few can withstand the wrath of the righteous.
"When one has witnessed the unspeakable, 'tis sometimes better to forget." —Vervamon the Elder
"May Svyelun and her tides favor you." —Traditional merfolk blessing
"Heed the lessons of our time: the forms of water may move the land itself and hold captive the fires within." —Gustha Ebbasdotter, Kjeldoran royal mage
"This school was founded in secret, operates in secret, and exists for the teaching of secrets. Those who would alter reality must first escape it." —Gerda Äagesdotter, Archmage of the Unseen
"Let them see what is not there and feel what does not touch them. When they no longer trust their senses, that is the time to strike." —Gerda Äagesdotter, Archmage of the Unseen
"While, like a ghastly rapid river, Through the pale door, A hideous throng rush out forever, And laugh—but smile no more." —Edgar Allan Poe, "The Haunted Palace"
"It was big. Really, really, big. No, bigger than that. It was big!" —Arna Kennerüd, skyknight
"Dwelling in icy mountain streams near goblin and orcish foes, the river merfolk were known for their stoicism." —*Sarpadian Empires, vol. V*
"No one can catch what won't be caught." —Kakra, sea troll
Fear the knight leaping from the water into the air, weapon ready.
"It was in Urza's journals that I finally found the secret at the core of the summonings." —Journal, author unknown
"Beast. Defiler. The source of all my pain." —Ihsan's Shade
Initially bred for sacrifice, the thrulls eventually turned on their masters, the Order of the Ebon Hand, with gruesome results. —*Sarpadian Empires, vol. II*
Battle doesn't need a purpose; the battle is its own purpose. You don't ask why a plague spreads or a field burns. Don't ask why I fight.
The thrulls bred at a terrifying pace. In the end, they overwhelmed the Order of the Ebon Hand.
"Strength it has, but at the cost of a continuous supply of energy. Such failure can bear only one result." —Execution order of Endrek Sahr, master breeder
Even the putrid muscles of the dead can provide strength to those loathsome enough to consume them.
Magic often masters those who cannot master it.
"We are not yet free of Lim-Dûl's terrors." —Halvor Arensson, Kjeldoran priest
"The lemures looked harmless, until they descended on my troops. Within moments, only bones remained." —Lucilde Fiksdotter, Leader of the Order of the White Shield
Knowing the hymn's power, the followers of Leitbur carefully guarded their pillaged transciptions.
"Expect my visit when the darkness comes. The night I think is best for hiding all." —Ouallada
"Phyrexia's touch is painful to all but the blackest of hearts." —Gerda Äagesdotter, Archmage of the Unseen
"Those idiots should never have bred thrulls for combat!" —Jherana Rure
"Until the Rebellion, thrulls served their masters faithfully—even at the cost of their own lives." —*Sarpadian Empires, vol. II*
The first line of defense against Urza and Mishra, the artifact blast achieved widespread fame until an unlucky mage discovered it was useless on the devices the brothers had already created.
"Peace will come only when we have taken Varchild's head." —Lovisa Coldeyes, Balduvian chieftain
Fire is never a gentle master.
The Crookshank military boasts a standing army of nearly twenty-four million, give or take twenty-two million.
"Often greatly outnumbered in battle, dwarves relied on catapults as one means of damaging a large army." —*Sarpadian Empires, vol. IV*
"Let no one say we did not fight until the last . . . ." —Headstone fragment from a mass grave found in the Crimson Peaks
"Must not all things at the last be swallowed up in death?" —Plato, Phædo, trans. Jowett
"Perhaps goblins are good for something after all." —General Khurzog
"According to accepted theory, the grenade held some kind of flammable mixture and was carried to its target by a hapless goblin." —*Sarpadian Empires, vol. IV*
If only it had three brains, too.

"While most overworlders fortunately don't realize this, gargoyles can be most delicious, providing you have the appropriate tools to carve them." —Asmoranomardicadaistinaculdacar, The Underworld Cookbook

"I was shocked when I first saw the aftermath of the Yavimaya Valley disaster. The raging waters had swept away trees, bridges, and even houses. My healers had much work to do." —Halvor Arenson, Kjeldoran priest
The Yeti's single greatest asset is its unnerving ability to blend in with its surroundings.
"Just the thing for those pesky water mages." —Jaya Ballard, task mage
"Striking silent as a dream, Cutting short the strangled scream . . ." —Tobrian, "Watchdragon"
What goes up, must come down.
"What tries to crush our spirit only strengthens our resolve." —Lovisa Coldeyes, Balduvian chieftain
"'Tis the set of sails and not the gales Which tells us the way to go." —Ella Wheeler Wilcox, "Winds of Fate"
"We must shake her limbs and rattle her brains." —Grandmother Sengir
"It had a mouth like that of a great beast, and gnashed its teeth as it strained to reach us. I am thankful it possessed no means of locomotion." —Vervamon the Elder
"Chub toad, chub toad At the door. Run away quick Or you'll run no more." —Traditional children's rhyme
"Living side by side with the elves for so long leaves me with no doubt that we serve the same goddess." —Kolbjörn, elder druid of the Juniper Order
"If the air must feed, let it take the self-righteous." —Murat, death speaker
"Fyndhorn is our home." —Kolbjörn, elder druid of the Juniper Order
"It's strange, but I can feel it when the land is corrupted. I understand why the Autumn Willow is so protective." —Daria
"That which nourishes can also bind." —Gemma, Willow Priestess
The only sound was the gentle clicking of the faeries' wings. Then those intruders who were still standing turned and fled. One thing was certain: they didn't think the Scryb were very funny anymore.
Freyalise forbid that any stranger should wander into the striders' territory.
"I hear there are bears—or spirits—that guard caravans passing through the forest." —Gulsen, abbey matron
Moss-covered statues littered the area, a macabre monument to the basilisk's power.
"The danger in cultivating massive plants caught the elves by surprise." —*Sarpadian Empires, vol. III*
"Blow, winds, and crack your cheeks! rage! blow!" —William Shakespeare, King Lear
"When one wolf calls, others follow. Who wants to fight creatures that eat scorpions?" —Maimun al-Wyluli, diary
"Few natural forces are as devastating as hunger." —Kaysa, elder druid of the Juniper Order
". . . And at his passing, the bodies of the world's great warriors shall rise from their graves and follow him to battle." —The Anvilonian Grimoire
"Centaurs will kill our aesthir if they can; they've always been enemies. Destroy the horse-people on sight." —Arna Kennerüd, Skyknight
"My power is as vast as the plains, my strength is that of mountains. Each wave that crashes upon the shore thunders like blood in my veins." —Dakkon Blackblade, Memoirs
"Relent, and you may transcend your situation." —Gerda Äagesdotter, Archmage of the Unseen
"There will come soft rains, and spring shall be amongst us, a welcome friend." —Halvor Arenson, Kjeldoran priest
Abandoning his sword to return to the lush forest of Pendelhaven, Jacques le Vert devoted his life to protecting the creatures of his homeland.
Ashnod found few willing to trade their humanity for the power she offered them.
Ashnod invented several torture techniques that could make victims even miles away beg for mercy as if the End had come.
Those who believed the city of Kroog would never fall to Mishra's forces severely underestimated the might of his war machines.
Valuing scholarship above all else, the inhabitants of the Ivory Tower reward those who sacrifice power for knowledge.
An early inspiration for Urza, Tocasia's onulets contained magical essences that could be cannibalized after they stopped functioning.
"Knowing its origins, how could they have thought they could control it?" —Sorine Relicbane, Soldevi heretic
"This shield is a true rarity: an artifact whose purpose is obvious." —Arcum Dagsson, Soldevi machinist
"My soldiers know that they need never fear for their protection." —King Darien of Kjeldor
The Pretender Mairsil ordered a great calendar drawn up to show when the paths to the Dark Lands were strongest.
Flawed copies of relics from the Thran Empire, the su-chi were inherently unstable but provided useful knowledge for Tocasia's students.
When sorely wounded or tired, Urza would often retreat to the workshops of his apprentices. They were greatly amazed at how much better he looked each time he took a sip of water.
"The fortress is not what it seems." —Arcum Dagsson, Soldevi machinist
"I will go to any length to achieve my goal. Eternal life is worth any sacrifice." —Zur the Enchanter
The Isle of Wak-Wak, home to a tribe of winged folk, is named for a peculiar fruit that grows there. The fruit looks like a woman's head, and when ripe speaks the word "Wak."
In the feudal days of Icatia, finding the Rainbow Vale was often the goal of knights' quests.
